record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares alternative flatness and other measured properties with held-out accuracy among trained networks, using different measures and settings from the specific version descriptions.
record.gate_note: The study's cited results about earlier flatness work are not recorded as rows. It reports its own rescaling experiment and cohort correlations; the latter include raw trace, relative flatness, margin, norm, and joint completion score.
record.test_reason: The text tests V1 in a new setting: the same MLP architecture and training protocol interpolate natural and fixed random MNIST labels, while Figure 1 shows natural-label test accuracy far above chance and random-label test accuracy near chance. The extracted correlation rows miss this result. The study does not test V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that raw Hessian trace depends on parameter coordinates, while joint completion score predicts accuracy in the two natural-label cohorts with a task-specific interpretation. Margin has larger correlation point estimates. They explicitly leave adjusted geometric measures open to evaluation; their results do not reject every flatness account. A common-task interpretation of the completion score also awaits the anchor-agreement audit.
record.recipe_differences: Uses frozen penultimate features, a joint affine-head feasibility bank, and correlations with held-out accuracy; cohorts are fixed-architecture multilayer perceptrons on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, not the convolutional settings described in V7. Includes function-preserving rescaling of ReLU networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported correlations; random-label training changes mean bank feasibility and removes the score-accuracy association. The paper says training sample and algorithm are fixed within cohorts and cautions that the result is conditional on them.

fits_no_version.finding: Joint completion score correlates positively with natural-label accuracy on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, but not with random-label accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under these fixed MLP protocols, joint affine-head feasibility tracks natural-label held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Raw Hessian trace and final-layer relative flatness have no multiplicity-corrected association with accuracy in either natural-label cohort.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These particular curvature measures do not reliably rank held-out accuracy in these low-data MLP cohorts.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral-product margin and smaller weight norm correlate with accuracy; margin has the largest correlation point estimate in each natural-label cohort.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin and norm predict accuracy under these fixed MLP protocols.

fits_no_version.finding: Function-preserving ReLU rescaling changes raw Hessian trace by up to 99-fold while preserving predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw Hessian trace is not invariant across parameterizations representing the same function.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean joint-bank feasibility is greater under random-label training than natural-label training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniform arbitrary-label completion feasibility depends on the training task and need not indicate useful classification generalization.

record.problems: The natural-label cohorts each use one fixed child set and training protocol, varying only training seed; the paper says results are conditional on that sample and algorithm. The networks are low-data MLPs on two datasets. The random-label comparison changes task, learned policy, representation, and relevant demand law. The study states that common-task interpretation additionally requires an anchor-agreement audit, which remains outstanding. Rescaling trace estimates use random vectors.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows left out. Table 6 reports feasibility by commitment order but does not measure a versioned claim outcome; Table 7 has individual trace values for one network, while R11 records the paper's aggregate rescaling result.

untested.parts: The original CIFAR-10 architectures and recipes, ImageNet/Inception V3, and incomplete random-label fitting on ImageNet. The new coexistence test concerns low-data MNIST MLPs.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond interpolation.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or learned-locality intervention.
No optimizer comparison or tuning-budget comparison.

No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance measurement or ranking of that measure against norms and margins. Raw trace and final-layer relative flatness are different constructs; function-preserving raw-trace rescaling does not refute V7.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

missing.what: Record the matched MNIST natural-label and random-label cohorts' perfect training classification and absolute held-out accuracies. Figure 1 places natural-label accuracies approximately at 72–82% and random-label accuracies at 9.4–10.8%; these are plot-read ranges, not reported cohort means. These outcomes establish the V1 comparison that correlation rows omit.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted numerical values agree with the supplied text. States marked cannot_determine concern the versioned effects, not the validity of the reported correlations. The record overlooks V1 evidence in the protocol and Figure 1 and overextends alternative curvature results to V7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare the same architectures trained on natural and random labels for natural-label generalization, or report that random-label networks fit nearly perfectly and have chance held-out accuracy.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.

Tests raw Hessian trace and final-layer relative flatness as correlates of held-out accuracy, and includes a function-preserving rescaling test. It does not test the stated magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance measure, convolutional-family comparisons, CIFAR-10 or SVHN, or data-augmentation conditions.
